nodes.text: Six releases of this newsroom, v0.1.5 to v0.1.10, landed on 25 September 2026 between 09:25 and 12:33 UTC
v0.1.5 was the first full newsroom run: the Journalist twice, the Historian, the Cartographer and the Editor
v0.1.6 captured the editor of record's flight notes as 45 issues: 8 epics, 33 tasks and 4 briefs, with a kanban in admin
v0.1.7 made issues a folder every desk may write and added tools/release.sh, which gates a release on every check
v0.1.8 shipped the approved front page, a sheet and byline on every piece, feedback everywhere, the reader's view and undo and redo
v0.1.9 shipped the principles, lessons markable one by one, a clickable and sortable network and a badge on every source page
v0.1.10 shipped a side pane on every page, briefing pages per target site and the first relayed message
30 run records carry the date 25 September: Build 9, Editor 6, Librarian 4, Journalist 4, Historian 2, Architect 2, editor of record 2, Cartographer 1
At the time of writing the issues folder holds 45 issues: 20 open, 23 done and 2 blocked, after this run's two moves
The notes file holds 35 notes in three groups: 12 on the site, 20 on content and 3 for agent@riskmandate.ai
The v0.1.5 commit body counts 8 new pieces, 124 decisions, 29 open questions, 6 map pages and 21 run records
The Build desk's run of 12:50 says the tier 1 chat is built and not run, because the session held no key
The Editor desk's run of 12:48 filed the relayed message under the riskmandate.ai briefing with status unsent
Sixteen issues moved to done across v0.1.8, v0.1.9 and v0.1.10: seven, five and four, by the Build desk's run records
The Editor desk's run of 12:09 counts 40 notes; a count of the bullet lines in the file gives 35
Principle 5 says the newsroom's releases, runs and issues are changes in the network, reported like any other site's
All eleven tags, v0.1.0 to v0.1.10, carry the same date in the git log: 25 September 2026
The Librarian has no changes file for 25 September, so the newsroom's own releases are not yet in the day's changes
Two of the six release commits carry a body with counts; four carry only their subject line
Which desk records the newsroom's own releases as changes, and from which file?
Does the notes file hold 35 notes or 40?
This piece is the first to carry briefing cards and a semantic twin, the two experiments its own subject filed
The newsroom can report on itself from its own files under the same rule as for any site: every claim linked
Round one of the twin experiment: this graph was written before the prose, and the prose from it
